text:
Alex: Heads up — after the nightly load runs we saw a 20% p95 latency regression on the hosted inference pool. Looking into parity between loadtest and prod.
Priya: Do we have a diff of GPUs / driver / CUDA between the two clusters? My hunch is kernel selection pulled a slower attention kernel.
Sam: Prod is A100s w/ driver 525.116 and CUDA 11.8. Loadtest was recently upgraded to different image using CUDA 12.1 + driver 535.86 on the staging A100 nodes.
Mei: Also noticed loadtest uses ubuntu:22.04 base image (libc 2.35) while prod is ubuntu:20.04 (libc 2.31) — container ABI might change fused-kernel picks.
perf-bot: quick profile summary (replay qps=200):
```
kernel attention_fused_v1: mean 0.9ms -> 1.3ms (x1.44)
kernel attention_split_v2: mean 1.1ms -> 0.9ms (fallback)
memcpy D2H increased by 24%
KV cache write spikes at sequence step 64
```
Priya: That matches: when CUDA runtime >=12 we fall back to split-attention path for certain seq-len alignments. KV cache layout + extra memcpy explains p95 tail.
Alex: So apples-to-apples would be same GPU model + driver + CUDA + container + kernel boot flags. Which flags did prod set? Any kernel cmdline tweaks?
Sam: Prod nodes boot with `transparent_hugepage=never` and cgroup v2 enforced, also `vm.swappiness=10`. Staging didn't set THP and was using older nvidia module params (no TCC tweaks).
Mei: We should standardize on `redwood/runtime:prod-2026-02` + driver 525.116 + CUDA 11.8 for the next comparison. Also pin `libcudnn=8.4.1` and `libcublas` ABI from the prod image.
Alex: Agreed. Action items: 1) Sam to repro loadtest with prod image + driver pin and attach new perf-bot profile; 2) Priya to run replay harness with identical traces across both envs (`./replay --input traces/2026-03-01.json --qps 200 --compare`); 3) Mei to create a terraform var that forces kernel cmdline flags for loadtest nodes.
Sam: I can run repro tonight. Quick command I'll use:
```
sudo docker run --gpus all --rm -e CUDA_VERSION=11.8 \
  -v /traces:/traces redwood/runtime:prod-2026-02 \
  ./replay --input /traces/2026-03-01.json --qps 200 --profile /out/profile.json
```
perf-bot: Tip: add `--trace-kv` to capture KV cache hits/misses, and include `--batch-stats` to emit batching distributions for apples-to-apples.
Priya: If we still see >10% p95 diff after that, we should check kernel selection logs in the runtime (enable `RUNTIME_DEBUG=kernel_selection`), and produce side-by-side kernel selection matrices.
Alex: Good plan. @Mei, can you also put a CI guard to fail merges that bump the test cluster image without a perf sign-off?
Mei: Yup, I'll add a quick check in the infra repo and post PR tomorrow.
Alex: Thanks team. Let's reconvene after Sam's run — please post perf-bot outputs to #eng-runtime.
